title: Yiadom and the Plant with a Secret

pages.text: In the school garden, the teacher knelt beside a patch of young weeds. “Wash your hands with soap after touching soil, and never taste any part of a plant,” she reminded the class. First, Yiadom tugged a small plant gently, and it held fast in the ground. Then the teacher loosened the damp soil carefully so Yiadom and Lobnibe could lift it out whole.
sentences: In the school garden, the teacher knelt beside a patch of young weeds.
“Wash your hands with soap after touching soil, and never taste any part of a plant,” she reminded the class.

pages.alt: In a Ghanaian school garden, a teacher in a patterned dress shows Yiadom and Lobnibe how to loosen damp soil and lift a small green plant whole.

pages.text: At the bottom of the lifted plant spread thin white threads. “Those are the roots,” said Lobnibe, looking closely. “That is why the plant held so firmly when you tugged it! Roots hold the plant in the soil and take in water.”

pages.alt: Yiadom holds up the small uprooted plant showing its clean white branching roots while Lobnibe inspects them closely.

pages.text: Back in class, the teacher placed the stem of a white flower into a glass jar of pink-coloured water. By the next morning, the tips of the white petals had turned pink! “The stem carries water up from the roots to the other parts,” she said. “It also holds the plant upright.”

pages.alt: On a wooden classroom table, Yiadom, Lobnibe, and their teacher lean in to admire a white flower in a glass jar of pink water with pink-tipped petals.

pages.text: “What do the leaves do?” asked Lobnibe, holding up her hand lens. The teacher smiled. “Leaves make food for the plant using sunlight, air, and water. You can think of a green leaf as the plant’s kitchen.” Yiadom smiled at the broad green leaves.

pages.alt: Lobnibe peers through a magnifying hand lens at the broad green leaves of the plant while Yiadom and their teacher watch beside a sunny window.

pages.text: At the top of the plant grew a small yellow flower. “The flower makes seeds,” said the teacher. “Later, those seeds can grow into new plants.” Outside the window, Lobnibe spotted a bee visiting a blossom. “Bees help carry pollen from flower to flower,” she said.

pages.alt: Outside the open classroom window, a golden honeybee hovers beside a small yellow garden flower while Yiadom and Lobnibe watch eagerly.

pages.text: The two friends painted the plant and pointed to every part in order. Then they shared their discovery: “Roots grow below because water is in the soil, and leaves spread up high where the sun shines.” “The place of each part fits its job!” said Yiadom.

activities.question: What do roots do?
options: Hold the plant firmly and take in water

activities.prompt: Put the parts in order, from the bottom of the plant upward.

activities.definition: The part of a plant that holds it upright and carries water.
